title: Visiting Myrtle Beach in winter
summary: What stays open, what slows down and how to enjoy the quiet season
description: What to do in Myrtle Beach in winter: which attractions stay open, what closes for the season, and how to plan around fewer crowds and cooler weather.
intro: Winter on the Grand Strand is quiet. The beaches are empty, hotel rates drop and traffic eases. It is not beach weather, but it can be a good time to visit if you plan for it.

p: A number of seasonal attractions close or run reduced schedules. Water parks and some amusement rides close for the season, a few mini golf courses have shortened hours, and some small tours and outfitters stop running. Rooftop and patio bars are often closed or quiet. Always check an attraction's own page before you drive over.

list: Golf. Winter is the cheapest time of year, and many courses stay open.
Indoor attractions like WonderWorks, Ripley's Aquarium, the Pinball Museum and escape rooms.
Live shows and dinner shows, many of which run holiday productions in November and December.
Breweries, wine bars and the live-music venues that stay open year-round.
Nature: state parks, Brookgreen Gardens and the MarshWalk are good in cool, clear weather, and Brookgreen is known for a winter light display.
Georgetown's museums and Harborwalk, for a day trip.

p: Dolphins swim along the coast all year, so a cruise is possible if a company is running trips. Schedules thin out in winter, so call ahead and ask what the weather policy is.

Bring layers. Winter days can be mild one afternoon and cold the next, and the wind off the water makes it feel colder. Plan outdoor things for the middle of the day and keep an indoor backup for each day.

Start late. Winter mornings are cold, and most outdoor attractions are at their best in the middle of the day. Have a slow breakfast, then take a walk at a state park or on the beach around late morning, when the air is warmest and the light is clear. The beach in winter is quiet and good for shell hunting, and you may have long stretches of it to yourself.

After lunch, move indoors. An aquarium, science museum or escape room fills the afternoon without worrying about the weather. Finish with a show or a meal. Holiday productions in November and December can be a highlight, and many theaters add extra performances.

From early November through the end of the year, the Grand Strand leans into the holidays. Theaters stage Christmas shows, resorts and gardens put up light displays, and towns hold parades and tree-lighting events. These are popular, so book tickets ahead if you want a specific night. Some businesses close on Thanksgiving, Christmas Day and New Year's Day, so confirm hours for those dates.

sections.h: Golf and outdoor sports in the cold months
p: Golf is the reason many winter visitors come. Courses stay open, rates are lower and the playing is comfortable on mild days, though frost delays can push back morning tee times. Ask about frost delay policy and bring layers. Tennis, pickleball and disc golf players also find the cooler weather pleasant, and bike paths and trails are quiet.

sections.h: Questions to ask before you drive anywhere
list: Is it open today? Many places run reduced weekday hours from November to March.
Is the outdoor part running? Boat tours, rides and mini golf may be weather-dependent.
Do I need a reservation? Smaller venues may only open for booked groups in the off-season.
What is the weather policy? Cold and wind can cancel cruises, and refunds vary.

p: Winter works for couples, retirees, golfers, anyone who wants a quiet trip and families who prefer indoor attractions. It is not the right choice if the main goal is swimming or water parks. For those, see our month-by-month guide and aim for summer.
